exhibits.lead: Software, physical AI, space technology—or something we haven’t imagined yet.
exhibits.body: We’re inviting developers, makers, startups and companies to share their interest in exhibiting at DevFest Indore. Bring a live demo, a working prototype or a product you’d love the community to experience.

themes.label: Space systems
themes.title: Your next input might come from orbit.
themes.description: A satellite sends a signal. A developer turns it into something useful. Explore the software between the two: telemetry pipelines, edge computing and working with data that can’t always phone home.

themes.label: AI agents
themes.title: Give your model a mission. And a way back.
themes.description: An agent can call tools, remember context and take action. The interesting part is making it dependable. Explore orchestration, evaluations and the human checkpoints that turn a clever demo into useful software.

themes.label: Physical AI
themes.title: The real world doesn’t have an undo button.
themes.description: When a model moves a machine, latency becomes distance and a wrong answer can become a wrong turn. Explore perception, robotics and the feedback loops that help intelligent systems act in a changing world.

themes.label: Cloud & systems
themes.title: Houston, we planned for this.
themes.description: Networks disappear. Traffic spikes. Hardware has other plans. Explore the architecture, data infrastructure and observability that keep systems useful when the happy path ends—on Earth or at the edge.

questions.question: What is GDG DevFest Indore 2026?
questions.answer: DevFest is an annual developer conference hosted by Google Developer Groups. The Indore edition brings developers, researchers, students and founders together for technical talks and hands-on learning.

questions.question: Who can attend DevFest?
questions.answer: Developers, researchers, students, tech leads, architects and founders are welcome. Choose a pass that matches your eligibility and the access you need.

questions.question: Are campus workshops part of the event-day program?
questions.answer: Campus workshops are separate events held before DevFest, with their own dates and registration details.

questions.question: Should I bring a laptop?
questions.answer: Bring your laptop and charger if you plan to join a hands-on lab. Setup instructions will be shared with the lab details.

questions.question: Which pass should I choose?
questions.answer: Students choose Cadet ({{studentPrice}}), issued through your campus ambassador. Working professionals choose Commander ({{professionalPrice}}), booked on the Tickets page. Both include the same sessions, workshop access, lunch, goodies and lounges.

questions.question: How do students get tickets?
questions.answer: Cadet tickets are issued through your campus ambassador or an organizer. Find your ambassador, ask for your Cadet pass, then complete registration on KonfHub with your college details. Bring your original student photo ID on the day.

questions.question: Is there a group discount?
questions.answer: Yes, for Commander. {{groupOffer}}. The discount applies automatically at KonfHub checkout. Each attendee still needs their own registration details.
